sentences.text: Platypterygius is a genus of Cretaceous ichthyosaurs with the name meaning "flat fin". Species assigned to this group were generally large-bodied macropredators characterized by robust teeth. The animal reached a length of approximately 7 meters and possessed a long snout and a powerful tail equipped with fins.
Platypterygius had more digits in its forefins than is usual for ichthyosaurs.
Several species of Platypterygius include described specimens of juveniles, newborns, and pregnant females.

In 1998, Arkhangelsky estimated that P. platydactylus was about 5 meters long and P. americanus was about 5.5 meters long. Later, in 2010, Zammit and colleagues estimated that P. australis was about 7 meters long.

While fossils of Platypterygius have been found on different continents, the holotype specimen was discovered in Germany. The type species was described in 1922 based on remains from Germany that had previously been described as Ichthyosaurus platydactylus in 1907 by Ferdinand Broili.
The original remains used to describe the type species were not adequately described and were destroyed during World War 2.
Like other ichthyosaurs, Platypterygius was viviparous.
Fossil evidence from P. australis includes hatchling protostegid sea turtles and enantiornithine birds found alongside fish in its gut contents.
A specimen of P. australis from Australia preserved gut contents of cephalopods, fish, and pterosaurs, as well as bite marks likely made by Kronosaurus queenslandicus.

Platypterygius was historically used as a wastebasket taxon, with many species likely being undiagnostic or representing distinct genera. Research in the 2000s and 2010s showed that the defining features of Platypterygius were either not present in all assigned species or were also found in other ophthalmosaurids.
An analysis by Zverkov and Jacobs (2020) showed that P. americanus is too distantly related to other species within the genus.
Platypterygius is the genus most closely related to Caypullisaurus and Brachypterygius.
